## Which Ecuador tours visit Cajas National Park?

[Cajas National Park](/ecuador/place/cajas-national-park/) lies in the Andes west of [Cuenca](/ecuador/place/cuenca/). Its defining features are a succession of high-altitude lakes, grassy páramo slopes and rapidly changing weather. On Ada Tours journeys, the park is usually visited while travelling from Cuenca to [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/), before the itinerary continues through other regions of Ecuador.

That makes it important to distinguish two goals when choosing a tour. One is **seeing the natural landscapes of Cajas as part of an extended journey across the country**. The other is **devoting separate time to a walking route**. Merely stopping in the park does not mean a long trek is included. Check the selected tour programme for the walking distance, trail and altitude demands.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} visiting Cajas as part of the main itinerary.

## How Cajas features in actual Ada Tours programmes

| Itinerary | Role of Cajas |
|---|---|
| [Ecuador for New Year](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) | Stop between Cuenca and Guayaquil |
| [Best of Ecuador](/ecuador/tour/best-of-ecuador-guaranteed-departures/) | Highlands plus a cacao hacienda |
| [Ecuador and the Galápagos, 17 days](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-adventure-17-days/) | Andean nature stop on a longer trip |

**The New Year itinerary** lasts 11 days and 10 nights. On the day spent at Cajas, travellers go from Cuenca through the high-altitude lake area towards Guayaquil, combining the natural landscapes with a visit to a cacao plantation. The group departure runs from 30 December 2026 to 9 January 2027. Choose it for the complete “Andes – coast – Galápagos” sequence, not solely for Cajas.

**“Best of Ecuador: Guaranteed Departures”** also includes a stop at the park on the way to Guayaquil. During that day, travellers discover the páramo, lakes and Tres Cruces viewpoint, then visit a cacao hacienda to learn about cultivating and processing cacao. This suits people who want to combine several natural environments with an introduction to local production.

**The 17-day Active Ecuador and Galápagos tour** passes through Cajas on day 13. The day includes high-altitude scenery, an introduction to the park's natural environment and the subsequent transfer to Guayaquil. Despite the overall tour's adventurous name, a visit to Cajas should not automatically be taken to imply a difficult hike: the exertion involved on that day needs separate confirmation.

To choose between these itineraries, consult the complete [Ecuador tour catalogue](/ecuador/tour/) and the selection of [Ecuador nature trips](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/).

## Cajas as a stop between Cuenca and Guayaquil

The road through the park links the Andean highlands with the route towards the Pacific coast. The transition has its own appeal: scenery changes from open grassy slopes and lakes to warmer landscapes as the road descends.

When planning the day, allow time for viewpoints, weather and travel. If the itinerary includes a cacao hacienda after Cajas, the day is shared among several activities. If your priority is a relaxed walk beside the lakes, discuss an additional day or a route adjustment rather than assuming a transit stop will become a full trekking excursion.

The park combines well with time in [Cuenca](/ecuador/place/cuenca/), and on longer journeys with the historic site of [Ingapirca](/ecuador/place/ingapirca/). These offer distinct experiences: colonial architecture, archaeology and highland natural scenery. Visiting all three in one day may be impractical without considerable travel.

## Walking trails, altitude and restrictions

Stopping at roadside viewpoints and following a dedicated hiking trail are more different than they may appear on a map. The official park operator ETAPA EP describes both short walking trails and more demanding routes. Around La Toreadora there are walks of different lengths, while highland routes run at approximately 3,800–4,000 metres or above.

Altitude can be felt even on short walks: the pace may slow, particularly after a rapid arrival in Ecuador by air. Bring warm waterproof clothing, wind protection and dependable footwear. If your itinerary includes an extended trek, discuss fitness and gradual acclimatisation to altitude in advance.

Park authorities recommend staying on marked paths, registering at designated checkpoints and avoiding long walks in bad weather. Swimming in the lakes is not advised. Check access rules for particular trails and permitted guiding arrangements before travelling.

**A practical criterion for choosing a tour:** its programme should explain how much time is allocated to the park, whether a trail walk is planned, where the day finishes and how onward transport works.

## Who should choose an itinerary including Cajas?

A route through Cajas suits travellers who want to see the Andean highlands without undertaking a separate multi-day expedition. It fits particularly well into a journey between Cuenca and Guayaquil when you want the road trip to include a natural highlight.

For someone whose main goal is an extended mountain trek, a single stop may not be enough. Choose a programme with more time in the mountains and check the physical demands, daily altitude and guiding arrangements. Travellers preferring minimal walking should agree on short scenic stops in advance rather than expecting a full hike.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Cajas

### How long does a visit to Cajas take?

It depends on the chosen route. In the three Ada Tours programmes, the park is visited during a transfer day between regions, so time is divided among travel and other activities. A separate hike needs specific arrangements.

### Can I see the lakes without a long hike?

Yes. A road runs through the park and there are viewpoints, although visibility depends on clouds and weather. A short stop is not a substitute for exploring the páramo ecosystem in depth.

### Is special equipment necessary in summer?

Warm waterproof clothing and suitable shoes are useful year-round: this is a high-altitude area with wind, fog and rain. For longer treks, confirm the equipment list for the particular trail.

### How do the three Cajas tours differ?

In their overall duration and the rest of their programmes. The [New Year itinerary](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) has fixed departure dates; the [guaranteed departures](/ecuador/tour/best-of-ecuador-guaranteed-departures/) combine Cajas with a cacao hacienda; the [17-day programme](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-adventure-17-days/) devotes more time to other parts of Ecuador and the Galápagos.

## Calderón in Ecuador: mazapán crafts on the road to Otavalo

[Calderón](/ecuador/place/calderon/) is an area north of Quito where the tradition of making decorative mazapán figurines continues. Artisans shape small people, animals, flowers and festive scenes from a flour-based mixture and then paint their creations carefully by hand. A visit adds an encounter with local crafts and the people keeping them alive to a journey through [Ecuador](/ecuador/).

The name mazapán may bring European almond marzipan to mind, but Calderón's products are **decorative figurines**, not desserts. They are made to decorate homes and preserve a cultural tradition. Visitors are particularly interested in the production process, from the malleable base to tiny painted details.

## How mazapán figurines are made

First, an artisan prepares a workable mixture of flour and other ingredients, shapes it and joins the parts. After drying or another processing stage, the figure is painted. Miniatures gain clothing, ornaments, hair, flowers and patterns; many details require a fine brush and patience.

Bright colours feature in the traditional palette. Common subjects include people in costume, animals, festive figures and miniature scenes from everyday life. Artisans have their own techniques, so handmade pieces retain individual features even when they depict similar themes.

Visiting a working craft studio differs from browsing souvenir shops. You can examine tools, understand the production stages and discuss the meaning of the figures. Arrange in advance whether production can actually be observed on the day: not every shop is a workshop open to visitors.

## Where the craft tradition came from

The history of the figures is connected to local customs, including commemorative rites around the Day of the Dead. Earlier items resembled ritual figures made of dough; over time, the craft evolved into durable decorative objects painted in vivid colours.

Ecuadorian municipal and government materials describe the tradition as part of Calderón's cultural identity. A modern souvenir, however, need not depict a religious or festive subject: workshops create a broad range of themes and personal designs.

When purchasing a miniature, ask about its origin and materials. Supporting an identifiable artisan and learning about the craft offers a deeper connection to local culture than buying an anonymous souvenir without a story.

## A museum and the preservation of the craft

In September 2026, the municipal outlet Quito Informa reported the creation of a museum in Calderón devoted to the area's history and mazapán tradition, with displays of historic objects and a space for activities. It offers another way to experience the craft within its cultural context, alongside the history of residents and other forms of handwork.

Before visiting, check current opening hours, exhibitions and whether classes are available. The existence of a museum project does not mean a museum visit is automatically included in a tour itinerary. Such a stop can be discussed separately during planning.

## Calderón, Guayllabamba and Otavalo: combining stops

Calderón lies on the northern route from [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) to [Otavalo](/ecuador/place/otavalo/). A craft stop can therefore be paired with a visit to the famous market and natural attractions in Ecuador's northern highlands.

The current [18-day Ada Tours trip through Ecuador and the Galápagos](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) includes Calderón and [Guayllabamba](/ecuador/place/guayllabamba/) en route to Otavalo. The first stop introduces dough figurines; the journey then continues with local produce and via [Miralago](/ecuador/place/miralago/) towards volcanic landscapes and Lake San Pablo.

Otavalo is known for textiles and its large market, while Calderón specialises in decorative miniatures. Combining them reveals 2 distinct craft traditions without turning the entire day into a shopping excursion.

## How much time to allow and what to confirm

A short stop provides enough time to explore a workshop or shop, but an in-depth conversation and demonstration call for a more relaxed pace. Decide in advance whether you want to see finished pieces, watch an artisan at work or participate in an activity if one is actually offered.

The area is in Ecuador's highlands. Comfortable shoes, sun protection and a light layer for changing weather are useful when travelling from the capital to Otavalo. The key questions concern the exact stopping point, studio opening hours and time needed for the onward transfer.

For travellers attracted by the region's cultural traditions, see the [“Culture and History” section](/interests/culture-and-history/). A cultural theme in a tour, however, does not imply that every workshop activity is included in the price.

## Frequently asked questions about Calderón

### Can Calderón's mazapán be eaten?

No. Modern figurines are generally made as decorations, sometimes using binding agents and paints. They must not be confused with confectionery marzipan.

### Where is Calderón?

North of Quito, along the road towards Otavalo. It makes a convenient cultural stop on a journey through Ecuador's northern highlands.

### Can visitors watch the figurines being made?

Some craft studios offer this, but the visit and demonstration must be arranged. Going into a shop does not guarantee meeting an artisan at work.

### Do Ada Tours itineraries stop in Calderón?

Yes. It is included in the [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) on the way to Otavalo.

## Which Ecuador tour visits Calderón?

[Calderón](/ecuador/place/calderon/) lies north of Quito and is known for its tradition of small painted dough figurines, locally called mazapán. The visit appeals to travellers who want to see a craft in practice: artisans shape and paint the figures by hand, turning a simple mixture into colourful miniatures.

In the current Ada Tours selection, Calderón is part of an [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos tour with a cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/). The stop takes place during the journey from Quito to [Otavalo](/ecuador/place/otavalo/) rather than occupying a full day. Within the itinerary, the craft theme complements Indigenous markets, Andean natural attractions and later stages of the trip.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Calderón on the main route. When choosing a trip, consider Calderón within the overall northern Ecuador programme: how much time is allowed for crafts, intermediate stops and walking around Otavalo.

## What is the mazapán craft?

In Calderón, *mazapán* refers to decorative figures traditionally made from a flour mixture, adhesives and pigments. They are not edible almond marzipan: the finished miniatures are souvenirs and examples of folk art. Local artisans make little people, animals, flowers and everyday scenes.

The craft's historical roots are associated with festive and memorial customs. Over time the items became brightly coloured decorative souvenirs. Seeing their production is more informative than only buying one: a workbench reveals the stages of shaping, drying, painting and finishing.

In September 2026, Quito's municipality reported on a museum and community workshops devoted to Calderón's cultural heritage. This is another reason to explore the area, but **a visit to a specific museum or hands-on workshop is not automatically included** in the Ada Tours itinerary and would require separate arrangements.

## A day from Quito via Calderón to Otavalo

On day 7 of the [18-day tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), travellers leave Quito heading north. The journey includes a stop in Calderón to discover the production of dough figurines. It then continues via [Guayllabamba](/ecuador/place/guayllabamba/) and Miralago, with views of Imbabura Volcano and [Lake San Pablo](/ecuador/place/san-pablo-lake/).

In [Otavalo](/ecuador/place/otavalo/), the itinerary visits the market on Plaza de los Ponchos, where locally made products, textiles and jewellery are displayed. The day continues to [Cotacachi](/ecuador/place/cotacachi/) and [Peguche Waterfall](/ecuador/place/peguche-waterfall/), followed by accommodation at a historic hacienda.

Calderón thus provides **an introduction to the crafts and culture of the northern route**. It differs from Otavalo, whose focus is the variety of the market and its products, and Cotacachi, which is known for leatherworking traditions. Each stop has its own purpose.

## How much time to set aside for Calderón

On our itinerary, the complete sightseeing day towards Otavalo takes approximately 8 hours, while the drive from Quito to Otavalo is about 2 hours excluding stops. The exact time spent with artisans is not specified separately.

If you mainly want to look at the figurines, a brief stop coordinated with the broader journey is sufficient. A full workshop or visits to several studios require additional time and confirmation of availability. Do not assume that a craft stop promises a hands-on class, the purchase of a particular item or a meeting with a named artisan.

During holidays and visits to working workshops, schedules should be confirmed separately. Ada Tours can help coordinate the order of stops while preserving time for Otavalo and the onward journey.

## Choosing a cultural route in northern Ecuador

If crafts and local traditions are your main interest, look for a programme including [Otavalo](/ecuador/place/otavalo/) and [Cotacachi](/ecuador/place/cotacachi/) as well as Calderón. [Peguche Waterfall](/ecuador/place/peguche-waterfall/) adds a natural experience to the day, while Lake San Pablo offers panoramic stops.

Travellers primarily interested in the Galápagos Islands should compare the full itineraries in the [Ecuador tour catalogue](/ecuador/tour/). Calderón alone is not the main purpose of the 18-day trip: it also includes the Amazon, cloud forests and a cruise. See [cultural and historical tours in Ecuador](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/ecuador/) for trips with different cultural emphases.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Calderón

### Is Calderón close to Quito?

Yes. It is an area in the northern part of the capital's metropolitan region, conveniently located on the route from Quito to northern Ecuador, including Otavalo.

### Are mazapán figurines edible?

The traditional decorative pieces for which Calderón is known are made for display, not eating. They should not be confused with confectionery marzipan or bread figures linked to other festive traditions.

### Does the tour include making your own figure?

The itinerary includes learning about the craft during a stop. A personal workshop and making a figurine yourself are not specified as included services and would require separate arrangements.

### Can Calderón and Otavalo market be visited on the same day?

Yes, this sequence is already part of the [18-day Ada Tours itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/). The day includes other stops, so the time at each depends on the overall schedule.

## Casa del Árbol: the Swing at the End of the World above the Baños valley

Casa del Árbol is a small viewpoint with a treehouse and the famous “Swing at the End of the World”, in the mountains above [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/), [Ecuador](/ecuador/). As someone swings out over the slope, clouds, forested valleys and Tungurahua Volcano form the backdrop. This unusual combination of a simple structure and mountain scenery has made the site famous in travel photographs.

The attraction is in the Runtún area, not in Baños's central square. Reaching it involves an uphill mountain road and extra time, particularly if you also want to visit waterfalls elsewhere in the valley.

## The history of the treehouse

The original treehouse is associated with Carlos Sánchez, a local resident who monitored Tungurahua Volcano. The lookout helped him track changes in the mountain's activity and conditions in the surrounding area. Later, the swing beside the treehouse became a popular tourist attraction.

Today, Casa del Árbol is a developed place for relaxation and photography. Cafés, viewpoints and other leisure attractions may operate on the grounds. The range of services depends on the current operation of the site, so do not assume that every activity is included in a standard admission.

## What you can see from the swing

On a clear day, you can see the Baños valley and the summit of Tungurahua Volcano. But mountain clouds sometimes hide the summit completely even when it is sunny in town. Plan the visit for the scenery and the outing itself, rather than treating a volcano view as guaranteed.

In photographs, the swing often appears suspended directly over a vast abyss. The actual sensation depends on the camera angle and the viewpoint's construction. Follow the operator's instructions when using the equipment, including weight limits and staff recommendations.

### Who might enjoy the visit?

The viewpoint can appeal to visitors with different levels of fitness. Choosing to use the swing or other attractions is a personal decision that calls for observing restrictions and assessing how you feel. Strong winds or bad weather may lead to limits on use.

For photographs, arriving ahead of large groups and leaving time for a short walk around the viewpoint can help. Queues for the swing are possible at busy times.

## Where Casa del Árbol is and how to get there

The complex is in Runtún above Baños, at an elevation of approximately **2,660 metres**. The official tourist guide for the Tungurahua region describes the uphill road from town and access by car, local transport or organised excursion.

The road winds up the mountainside, so account for bends, cloud and possible rain. Not every stretch is suitable for a leisurely walk on foot from town. When choosing transport, also plan your return journey and possible waiting time.

Admission prices, additional activities and opening hours may change. Check them directly with the site, especially before visiting on a weekend or public holiday.

## What to combine with Casa del Árbol near Baños

Baños is known for nature excursions in the Pastaza River valley. The most recognisable sights include [Pailón del Diablo Waterfall](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/) and [Manto de la Novia](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/). Casa del Árbol lies above town and offers a different experience: mountains and sky instead of the force of falling water in a gorge.

Several sights can be combined in one day, but this requires transport along different roads. If you would like more time at the swing, it makes sense to treat it as a separate stop rather than rushing between every waterfall.

## Casa del Árbol on Ada Tours itineraries

Our [New Year programme “All of Ecuador: Andes and Galápagos”](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) includes Casa del Árbol on its route across the country. The [“Ecuador, Galápagos and Humpback Whales” tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/) also features it in the Baños portion of the itinerary.

These tours cover several different regions, so the swing is only one stop. Check rules for using the attraction and the availability of optional activities against the schedule for the relevant day. For alternatives, browse [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/).

## When to go and what to bring

Mornings may offer more open views, although clear mountain weather can never be guaranteed. Even on a warm day it can be cool and windy at altitude, and paths may become slippery after rain. Shoes with good traction, a rain jacket, sun protection and water are useful.

If your main goal is a photograph on the swing, check that the attraction will be operating on the day of your visit and that staff can arrange safe boarding. Do not try dangerous poses merely to reproduce a photograph.

## Frequently asked questions about Casa del Árbol

### Where is the Swing at the End of the World?

In the mountains of the Runtún area near Baños, Ecuador, at Casa del Árbol.

### Can Tungurahua Volcano be seen from the swing?

It may be visible in clear weather. Cloud cover changes frequently, so a view of the summit is not guaranteed.

### Can I visit without an excursion?

Yes, there is a road to the site. Arrange transport both ways and check the opening hours in advance.

### Is it an extreme sport?

Visiting the viewpoint is a tourist activity, while use of the swing requires observing its safety rules. It is different from demanding mountain trekking or a sporting descent.

## Tours visiting the Swing at the End of the World in Ecuador: choosing a route

**Casa del Árbol is well worth including in a journey through Baños and the Andes.** The Swing at the End of the World sits beside a treehouse high above the valley. In good visibility, the surrounding mountains and the area around Tungurahua Volcano can be seen from here. The attraction is chiefly about the panorama and a short stop, so the overall Ecuador itinerary matters more when choosing a tour than the duration of the visit itself.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that visit [Casa del Árbol](/ecuador/place/casa-del-arbol/) on the main route. Both connect [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) with other parts of the country, but differ significantly in departure dates and final experiences.

## Comparing two journeys featuring Casa del Árbol

### New Year: the Andes and the Galápagos Islands

[“All of Ecuador for New Year: Andes and Galápagos”](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) is an 11-day journey. Its Andean section includes [Quilotoa crater lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/), Baños and a series of waterfalls before continuing to other mainland cities and the Galápagos Islands.

The swing is included on the day exploring Baños and travelling through the Pastaza River valley. The itinerary also mentions [Agoyán Waterfall](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/), [Manto de la Novia](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/) and [Pailón del Diablo](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/). Combining them lets travellers see several natural sights in one day, but leaves less time at each than a separate multi-day stay in Baños would.

This itinerary is designed around the holiday season and includes drives through the country's mountains. Check the accommodation arrangements and the daily schedule to assess how demanding the journey will be.

### August: the Andes, Galápagos and whale watching

The [“Ecuador, Galápagos and Humpback Whales” tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/) also lasts 11 days, but runs from 11 to 21 August 2027. Its opening days visit Quito, Quilotoa and Baños, followed by the islands and the Pacific coast.

Here Casa del Árbol is part of the Baños day, together with [Pastaza Canyon](/ecuador/place/pastaza-canyon/) and a return to Quito. The day involving transfers lasts 11–12 hours, so adding extra excursions without adjusting the schedule is not advisable. The final section includes time by the ocean and a trip to see humpback whales; sightings depend on natural and weather conditions.

**The distinction lies not in the swing itself, but in the sequence and seasonal purpose of each trip.** New Year suits travellers wanting to spend the holiday in Ecuador; the August route suits those drawn to the combination of the Andes, Galápagos and an ocean programme featuring whales.

## What the Casa del Árbol visit involves

The viewpoint is on the slopes above Baños. The well-known treehouse was built around a tree, and the swing faces the mountain scenery. The stop pairs easily with other sights nearby, while the [“Waterfall Route”](/ecuador/place/banos/) helps explain why Baños has become a popular centre for nature excursions.

Visitors come for photographs and valley views, but **the panorama depends on cloud cover**. You may arrive on an overcast day when the mountains are almost completely hidden. A specific volcano view or perfect photograph on your chosen date cannot be promised.

Using the swing requires a separate personal decision. If you would rather admire the view without riding, make that clear when arranging the excursion; visiting the viewpoint and using the swing are different activities. Current safety requirements, queues and admission rules are determined on site.

## What to check when booking a tour through Baños

**Transfer day.** The route to Baños crosses several mountain sections. Both current itineraries include Casa del Árbol on a busy day with other stops. Consider not only how long you have at the viewpoint but also when you reach your hotel in the evening.

**Altitude and weather.** The road via Quilotoa takes travellers into the highlands, while Baños lies lower. Layered clothing, comfortable shoes and rain protection are useful for these changes. Consider how you feel after the drive and any personal limitations concerning climbing or altitude.

**Galápagos and the coast.** If island wildlife is your principal goal, compare the number of days on the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and the actual programme of visits. The brief stop at the swing should not determine your choice of a long itinerary on its own.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring Casa del Árbol

### Is Casa del Árbol a standalone tour from Quito?

In these Ada Tours programmes, it is **one stop** on the Andean section of a longer journey. The Baños day includes other natural attractions and road transfers.

### Can the swing and waterfalls be seen in one day?

Yes. Both tours combine Casa del Árbol with natural sights in the [Baños area](/ecuador/place/banos/). The exact time at each depends on road conditions and the schedule.

### Is a view of Tungurahua guaranteed?

No. Visibility depends on cloud and weather. Choose the trip for its complete itinerary and treat the panorama as a welcome possibility that nature cannot guarantee.

### Which is better: the New Year or August itinerary?

Compare the convenience of the dates and the final stage of the journey. The [New Year tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) focuses on a festive trip through the Andes to the islands; the [August programme](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/) adds the coast and whale watching.
